issues.legal_issue: Forfeiture of an auction purchaser’s deposit during the sale of secured assets is part of the secured creditor’s recovery measures, and an aggrieved auction purchaser may challenge it before the recovery tribunal.
material_facts: A secured creditor auctioned a borrower’s secured assets after the borrower defaulted on its loan.
The highest bidder’s offer was accepted, but the bidder failed to pay the sale instalments as agreed.
The secured creditor forfeited the bidder’s deposit following that default.
The bidder challenged the forfeiture, and the dispute concerned whether the tribunal could review that action as part of the secured-asset sale process.
issues.conclusion: The forfeiture was part of the measures taken to enforce the security, and the auction purchaser, as an aggrieved person, could challenge it before the tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13(4) and 17 of the SARFAESI Act, read with Rules 8 and 9 of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002, make the sale process and its completion part of the secured creditor’s enforcement measures. Rule 9(5) expressly provides for forfeiture when the purchaser defaults on payment. Section 17 permits any aggrieved person to challenge those measures, including actions taken under the relevant Rules. The Court distinguished Umang Sugars Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra & Anr., 2014(4) Mh.L.J. 113, because that decision did not consider the Rules and their effect.

rule.if: secured_asset_recovery_sale_proceeding and auction_purchaser_defaulted_on_payment and creditor_forfeited_deposit_during_sale_process and purchaser_aggrieved_by_forfeiture

predicates.secured_asset_recovery_sale_proceeding: A secured creditor pursued recovery by selling assets given as security for a borrower’s debt.
predicates.auction_purchaser_defaulted_on_payment: The successful auction purchaser failed to pay the sale price as agreed.
predicates.creditor_forfeited_deposit_during_sale_p: The secured creditor forfeited the purchaser’s deposit as a consequence of the payment default during the sale process.
predicates.purchaser_aggrieved_by_forfeiture: The purchaser objected to the forfeiture and sought to challenge it.

issues.definition: When a purchaser defaults during a secured-asset sale and the creditor forfeits the deposit as part of that sale process, an aggrieved purchaser can seek tribunal review of the forfeiture.

issues.legal_issue: A writ petition challenging a secured creditor’s recovery action should ordinarily not be entertained when an effective statutory remedy is available to challenge that action before the recovery tribunal.
material_facts: The auction purchaser filed a writ petition challenging the secured creditor’s forfeiture of its deposit.
The forfeiture could be challenged before the recovery tribunal through an effective statutory remedy.
The writ court dismissed the petition without deciding the forfeiture’s merits, and the appellate court upheld that dismissal.
No reason was found in this case to depart from the ordinary rule of requiring recourse to the statutory remedy.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in dismissing the writ petition because the purchaser could challenge the forfeiture before the tribunal; the purchaser was granted liberty to pursue that remedy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act provides an effective remedy before the tribunal for an aggrieved person challenging measures under Section 13(4). Under United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon & Ors., (2010) 8 SCC 110, a High Court will ordinarily not entertain a petition under Article 226 when an effective alternative remedy is available, with particular restraint in matters concerning recovery of public dues and bank debts. Exhaustion is a rule of discretion, not compulsion, but the statutory remedy should ordinarily be used first.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_dismissal and writ_challenges_secured_creditor_recovery_action and effective_tribunal_remedy_available and no_exceptional_reason_to_bypass_remedy

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The proceeding is an appeal from the dismissal of a writ petition.
predicates.writ_challenges_secured_creditor_recover: The writ petition challenges an action taken by a secured creditor in recovering a debt.
predicates.effective_tribunal_remedy_available: An effective statutory process before a tribunal is available to challenge the creditor’s action.
predicates.no_exceptional_reason_to_bypass_remedy: No exceptional reason is shown for bypassing the available statutory process.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns dismissal of a writ petition challenging a creditor’s recovery action, and an effective tribunal remedy is available with no exceptional reason to bypass it, the writ petition should ordinarily await use of that remedy.
